headline: High-risk shared git workspace and broad egress create default data-leakage and cascading-error exposure; prompt-injection risk is lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes git-tracked files and can execute shell commands; Chatwoot exposes API integrations and broad network egress. If Chatwoot content is copied into Aider-managed files, Aider may treat attacker-controlled text as instructions. The pair lacks explicit provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible but not default-automatic.
conditions: IF Chatwoot-generated content is pasted into files Aider edits
IF Aider is instructed to follow instructions embedded in repository text
mitigations: Keep Chatwoot exports out of Aider-managed repos
Add a manual review step before Aider applies file changes
Prefix imported support text with a non-executable delimiter
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to content passed between systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider has broad network egress and handles model-provider API keys while reading/writing repository files; Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, messages, and reports. If customer records or transcripts enter the shared repo or Aider context, they can be transmitted to third-party model providers. The blast radius includes sensitive customer data and is dangerous in default workflows.
conditions: IF customer data, messages, or reports are placed in the shared repository
IF Aider forwards those files into a configured external model provider
mitigations: Exclude customer data from the shared repo
Redact transcripts before Aider reads them
Use a local-only model backend for Aider
Rotate any exposed provider keys
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on repo inputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider can write the filesystem and modify git state, and its concurrency model explicitly shares state via a shared git repo. Chatwoot is not shown as writing the same repo, but if it does via integrations or operator workflows, concurrent edits can collide and corrupt git history. Because the shared mutable surface is explicit on Aider and the other side has broad egress/integration surfaces, uncertainty should escalate.
conditions: IF Chatwoot writes artifacts into the same git repository Aider edits
IF both systems modify the same files or branches without locking
mitigations: Use separate branches per agent
Require one writer at a time
Run a pre-merge diff review
Freeze Chatwoot-generated files before Aider edits them
requires-engineering: add repository locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can generate code changes and commits, while Chatwoot can surface customer-facing content through integrations. If Chatwoot output is treated as authoritative input to Aider, or Aider-generated text is forwarded into support workflows, errors can cascade across work products. There is no documented verification bridge, so the pathway exists but is not proven default-dangerous.
conditions: IF Chatwoot output is copied into Aider without human verification
IF Aider-generated content is published into customer-support workflows
mitigations: Require human approval before forwarding outputs
Check Aider changes against source tickets
Limit Chatwoot-to-Aider transfers to summaries only
Mark generated text as untrusted until reviewed

E_compliance.rationale: Aider is documented as handling source code and git history, while Chatwoot handles customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, and messages. If customer-support data is moved into Aider-managed repositories, retention and residency obligations can diverge from Chatwoot’s support system. The profiles do not specify a residency mismatch, so this is a compliance-gap risk rather than a breach certainty.
conditions: IF customer messages or contact profiles are stored in the shared git repo
IF retention or deletion requests must be honored across both systems
mitigations: Keep customer data out of git history
Pseudonymize support artifacts before export
Document retention ownership for each system
Purge accidental commits quickly
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows
